newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli inflation-linked bonds end higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli inflation-linked bonds end higher.

text.p: Most Israeli bonds closed higher on Tuesday led by a rise in debt instruments linked to the consumer price index (CPI), traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.04 pct to 169.74.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct to 160.52
"Bonds continue to rise but on a much slower pace," said a trader at Bank Hapoalim.
Overall volume was low at 129 million shekels as unlinked bonds came to what traders said was a saturation point.

"Prices for unlinked bonds have...reached a ceiling and the rise was very moderate today. The unlinked bonds reflect hopes for a rate cut of 0.3 percentage points," Ron Weisberg at I.B.I. Investment House said.
The Bank of Israel will announce its short-term interest rates for December on Monday. Its key lending rate is currently at an annual 15.2 percent.
"Most of the activity is still concentrated in the CPI-linked bonds. The Bank of Israel issued very few (of these) bonds lately and demand continues to rise," Weisberg said.
Traders noted that yields on inflation-linked long bonds fell below 4.5 percent, a level at which the market is expected to stabilise.
The trader at Hapoalim said Makams were also stable as yields on one-year Makams fell to 15.15 percent. Activity in the Makams was low at 26 million shekels.
"The Makams' prices will not rise much further. Prices are expected to remain stable with yields of 15 percent," Weisberg said.
Dollar-linked bonds declined slightly in thin and mixed trading.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
